newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Safras to acquire Mizrahi's New York subsidiary.
newsitem.headline: Safras to acquire Mizrahi's New York subsidiary.

text.p: Safra National Bank of New York and United Mizrahi Bank of Israel announced on Thursday that they have signed an agreement for the sale of Mizrahi's U.S. subsidiary to Safra for about $30 million.
The transaction is subject to regulatory approval, which is expected to be obtained in several months.
The sale of the overseas operation is part of the Israeli bank's privatisation.
Mizrahi, Israel's fourth largest bank, was privatised last year with the Ofer Wertheim groups acquiring a controlling 26 percent stake with an option for an additional 25 percent.
The bank has total assets of $14 billion while its U.S. subsidiary United Mizrahi Bank and Trust Co of New York (UMB N.Y.) has assets of $300 million.

Safra National Bank of New York, with assets of $1.5 billion, is owned by Joseph and Moise Safra, the Brazilian bankers who control the First International Bank of Israel They also own Banco Safra, a Brazilian bank with $8.6 billion in assets.

The agreement includes the transfer of Mizrahi's interests in its representative offices in Latin America. The agreement allows Mizrahi to continue servicing its private banking customers through the bank in Israel and its remaining affiliates abroad.
"Mizrahi Bank continues to be committed to further developing its international private banking services to foreign residents," said Victor Medina, managing director of Mizrahi.

David Kimche, UMB N.Y.'s chairman, said the transaction reflected the bank's success "in restructuring and building up quality business of the bank after it had been adversely affected by the deep real estate depression in New York in the late eighties".

Safra National had total stockholders' equity of $75 million and total deposits of $1.2 billion as of September 30 while UMB N.Y. had total stockholders' equity of $21.5 million and deposits of $260 million.
Commercial Bank of New York, which is controlled by Brazilian banker Edmundo Safdie, had also sought to buy Mizrahi's U.S. subsidiary.
